26-## Stability
27-
28:New releases come out many times a day, but the install command below gives you the **stable channel**: a release reaches it only after the full test suite and a two-hour, 600,000-page load test pass on that exact release, and only when an important fix is waiting or stable is a week old. Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. [docs/STABILITY.md](docs/STABILITY.md) explains that promise, how often stable moves, how to pin a version or go back, and what the faster alpha channel is for.

31-
32-> [!TIP]
33-> **Fastest: hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/cli?ref=readme), for any harness.** One command launches a GBrain hosted on gbrain.io; Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor and every other AI you use connect to it, with nothing to keep online.
34->

37-> gbrainio terminal connect      # in a new terminal
38-> gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
39:> curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
40-> export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
41:> bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
42-> # Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
43-> (claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only
44-> # Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
45-> (codex mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || codex mcp add gbrain --url https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup codex --instructions-only
46-> ```
47->
48:> Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#no-unzip), not an improvised one. A command scanner (Hermes) refuses the Bun installer or `bun install -g`? Use the [release binary route](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#release-binary).
49->
50-> `gbrain setup <harness> --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. It writes the [brain-first block](docs/guides/setup.md#brain-first-instructions) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out.
51->
52:> The installer is a shell script for macOS and Linux; read it before you run it.

83-
84:Hermes checks every shell command before it runs it, and with nobody there to approve (`hermes chat -q`, a gateway or cron run) it refuses the Bun installer and `bun install -g`. Install the release binary instead, one file that needs no Bun and no package install, and let setup register it through Hermes's own `hermes mcp add`. 93-Then start a new Hermes session. Setup registers the MCP server (`hermes mcp test gbrain` checks it) and adds the brain-first rule to `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` with a per-turn hook. Hermes's approval and command-scanner settings stay as they are; setup only records the approval for its own per-turn hook. If setup prints a `hermes mcp add` command instead of registering, run that command as printed. To paste it to Hermes instead, use the prompt above. Details: [docs/mcp/HERMES.md](docs/mcp/HERMES.md).

content.text: 200 # Connect GBrain to OpenClaw > This page is the MCP-registration reference card. For the full brain install > — CLI, engine, skills, dream cycle — follow > [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md); the README covers the > bootstrap and connect paths. Connect with [Option 2](#option-2-openclaw-mcp-add) (stdio) when the brain runs on the gateway's machine, or with [OpenClaw's own MCP client](#remote-brain-openclaws-mcp-client-over-https) when it runs elsewhere. Option 1's ClawHub bundle is not available yet. A bot that several people DM connects over HTTP as well: see [One bot for several people, in DMs](#one-bot-for-several-people-in-dms). ## Option 1: ClawHub bundle plugin (not available yet) This project publishes no ClawHub package yet. The package named `gbrain` on ClawHub is an unofficial upload of an old 0.10.1 build whose manifest has no `id`, so `openclaw plugins install clawhub:gbrain` stops with `plugin manifest requires id`. Don't install it; use Option 2. GBrain ships [`openclaw.plugin.json`](../../openclaw.plugin.json) at the repo root. Installing the bundle plugin registers the MCP server for you — the manifest carries an `mcpServers.gbrain` entry that runs the bundled `.agents/gbrain-launcher serve` (the same launcher the Codex and Claude Code plugins use; it resolves your installed `gbrain` via `GBRAIN_BIN`, then `~/.bun/bin/gbrain`, then `PATH`, so it works under launchd's bare PATH and never needs a build step) plus the bundled skills — and declares the `gbrain-context-engine` context engine. To route OpenClaw's context-engine slot through gbrain, two steps, in this order: 1. Install and enable the plugin by its own id, `gbrain-context-engine` (the `id` in `openclaw.plugin.json`). 2. Set the slot to the engine id the plugin registers: ``` plugins.slots.contextEngine = gbrain-context-engine ``` The current host requires the canonical plugin ID in the slot. The installed plugin ID is unchanged and `gbrain-context` remains a registry alias for older integrations, but it is not a slot alias on current hosts: migrate an old `plugins.slots.contextEngine = gbrain-context` setting to `gbrain-context-engine`. Setting the slot alone does not install/enable the plugin. For a legacy host that cannot provide a per-session workspace, set `plugins.entries.gbrain-context-engine.config.workspaceDir` to an absolute workspace path; on multi-agent hosts prefer the host-supplied workspace. An unbound or ambiguous workspace warns and reads no source rather than selecting an arbitrary agent's memory. The factory also accepts zero arguments from current hosts. Its `assemble` keeps the current prompt separate from fenced stored transcript history; an identical trailing legacy user message is already the current turn. The admitted-turn acknowledgement is stateless and writes nothing. Reflex-only pointer synthesis leaves returned messages unchanged; the turn acknowledgement does not automatically capture conversation content (compaction has its own explicit checkpoint path). Loading the plugin alone is not evidence of model recall: verify saved-page retrieval after a restarted turn and source isolation with the intended host. The loopback native test uses a deterministic provider, so it does not certify paid-model recall or provenance. 9:> curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed 11:> bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain 18:> Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. 56:> missing `github:` prefix is the trap). Install only `github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` 65:Default path (Bun 1.4.4 or newer is required — gbrain is a Bun + TypeScript runtime; on an older Bun, run `bun upgrade` first): 70:bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable 76:Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. 78: 88:bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable 862:[stable channel](docs/guides/upgrades-auto-update.md#stable-channel)).

I installed gbrain v0.60.760.0. Running `gbrain --version` in a new login shell prints `gbrain 0.60.760.0`. It was installed from commit `1597b77`, which is the commit the `v0.60.760.0` tag points to.

**What I did:**
- **Install command:** everywhere the docs say `#stable`, I used `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.760.0` instead. The `stable` tag currently points to a different commit (`3e3f6a2`), so this install is not the stable channel.
- **Bun:** gbrain needs Bun 1.4.4 or newer, and it wasn't installed. The normal Bun installer needs `unzip`, which is missing, and there's no root or sudo here to add it. So I used the docs' "no-unzip" route instead. It put Bun 1.4.4 in `~/.bun/bin` and added that folder to the PATH in `~/.profile`.
- **Location:** the `gbrain` command is at `/harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain`.

**Not done yet:** this only installs the command-line tool. There's no brain set up and nothing connected to OpenClaw. The docs' next steps are:
- **Create the brain:** `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`
- **Connect it to OpenClaw:** register it as an MCP server using "Option 2" in the gbrain guide `docs/mcp/OPENCLAW.md`. Don't use the `gbrain` package on ClawHub: it's an unofficial upload of an old version and fails to install.

I can do both if you want.
